passages.note: Bill text conditions registration on documentary proof of citizenship, matching rung 5.
House Third Reading vote where Hoffman voted Y, but this was his own act as a State Representative, not as State Senator.
Bill history lists Hoffman as Prime sponsor of HB2492, signed into law before his Senate term began.

rows.reasoning: HB2492 (2022) is chair-shaped for rung 5 (it conditions registration on documentary proof of citizenship), and Hoffman was its prime sponsor and a Yea vote in the House. But the bill was introduced, passed, and signed in 2022, while Hoffman held a different office (State Representative), before his State Senate term began 2023-01-02; per V5 a record from an earlier office is valid for that office only, so none of these passages can establish the chair for this State Senator row.
